source.title: Deep Networks Always Grok and Here is Why
source.authors: Ahmed Imtiaz Humayun; Randall Balestriero; R. Baraniuk

record.tranche_reason: Tests grokking-like delayed behavior and its proposed local-complexity mechanism in additional settings, including image and Shakespeare-text tasks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for test accuracy, adversarial accuracy, and local complexity. It also discusses prior studies, which are not recorded as results here. Several outcomes are described in text while their curves are shown only in figures.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own grokking runs: scaled-init MNIST MLP, a modular-addition transformer, and a continuous progress measure (local complexity) timed against grokking onset. Most headline results are 'delayed robustness', meaning late gains in adversarial accuracy after clean test accuracy has already converged. That is a related but different construct from delayed test generalization.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors claim grokking is widespread and not restricted to particular tasks or initialization. However, their realistic-data evidence is delayed robustness, not delayed test generalization. They attribute both delayed generalization and delayed robustness to a late 'region migration' phase of local-complexity descent. They report that batch norm removes adversarial grokking, and they acknowledge they lack a theoretical explanation for why migration occurs late.
record.recipe_differences: Rather than reproducing the original algorithmic grokking setup, the study measures local complexity and evaluates adversarial accuracy across image, text, and algorithmic settings; it also varies architectural and training parameters.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch normalization removes or significantly delays the reported adversarial grokking; initialization scaling by eight induces visible grokking; changing weight decay can either delay or hasten region migration; increasing training-set size hastens grokking in the reported MNIST setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Delayed robustness: adversarial (PGD, AutoAttack) accuracy rises long after training and clean test accuracy converge. Shown for MNIST MLP, CIFAR10/100 CNN, ResNet18 on CIFAR10/Imagenette, and a char-level GPT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Networks show grokking-like delayed gains in adversarial robustness after test accuracy saturates, across image and text settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Interventions on delayed robustness: batch norm removes it or significantly delays it; larger training sets, width, depth and batch size hasten it; randomly labelled data and weight decay delay region migration.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The timing of delayed robustness and LC region migration depends on batch norm, data size, parameter count and regularization.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235, 2024
record.problems: The paper states that it lacks a theoretical justification for the double-descent local-complexity behavior. Many accuracy trajectories are presented in figures without exact values in the text. The local-complexity measure is an approximation, and the paper does not directly identify the specific generalizing or memorizing circuits described in V2.

untested.parts: How the delay scales with training-set size on algorithmic data; the actual size of the accuracy jump (figure only).
Identification of a Fourier or other generalizing circuit and removal of memorizing components. Only an informal link to Nanda's cleanup phase is drawn (Fig 24).
Molecules; weight norm as the switch; the lazy-to-rich framing; test-set grokking on CIFAR/Imagenette/text.
Realistic LLM pretraining or fine-tuning not tested.
Circuit efficiency, critical dataset size, ungrokking: none measured on test-set grokking.
Adam is used throughout. The authors note only Adam was studied; there are no optimizer or precision controls.

missing.what: Clean test accuracy converges before the adversarial grokking in the standard-init image and text runs. The paper says networks grok adversarial samples 'long after generalizing on the test dataset'. This is direct evidence of no test-set delay in these settings.
missing.locator: Section 1 Observation; Fig 1 caption; Fig 9 caption; Fig 33

missing.what: Fig 2 / Fig 7 caption: the standard-init MNIST MLP does not undergo delayed generalization. This is the needed baseline for the init-scale run in R9.

record.verdict_notes: Title and abstract overstate the result: 'grokking' on CIFAR10 and Imagenette refers to adversarial accuracy. I treated delayed robustness as a different construct from V3's delayed generalization; reviewers may disagree. Only R1 (modular addition, figure-only) and R9 (scaled init) involve test-set grokking. R11's setting is internally inconsistent between the text, the Fig 30 caption and Table 1.

versions.untested_parts: The modular-addition result is reported, but the paper does not test how the delay changes as the training set shrinks.
Local complexity and region migration are measured, but the paper does not directly identify a Fourier algorithm or track the formation and removal of specific memorizing circuits.
Tests image and Shakespeare-text settings and initialization scaling. It does not test molecules or establish a lazy-to-rich transition; it does not directly measure weight norm as the switch.
The GPT-based model is trained on Shakespeare text, but this is not a test of realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning.
Weight decay and training-data size are varied, but the paper does not test circuit efficiency, a critical dataset-size threshold, or ungrokking below such a threshold.
The paper does not compare whether different runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm.
The paper uses Adam but does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point/softmax artifacts with controlled alternatives.

rows.subject: Transformer architecture (modular addition; architecture details not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Measured training and test accuracy and local complexity during training.
rows.measure: Training/test accuracy and local complexity over optimization steps
rows.note: The authors state that region migration occurs during grokking in this setting. The figure shows accuracy and local-complexity trajectories, but the text gives no exact accuracy values or delay.
rows.check: Figure only. The text says only that region migration occurs during grokking (Fig 8). No accuracy values, delay length or data-size dependence are given. The paper also says this setting shows its delayed-robustness phenomenon, so what Fig 8 plots cannot be fully checked from the text.

rows.subject: DNNs in the reported delayed-generalization and delayed-robustness experiments
rows.operation_detail: Measured local complexity around training, test, and random points over training.
rows.measure: Local-complexity dynamics relative to delayed generalization or robustness
rows.value: The authors state that the second descent always precedes the onset of delayed generalization or delayed robustness.
rows.uncertainty: 99% confidence intervals are shown for local-complexity plots; numerical interval values not stated.
rows.note: This is a progress measure and temporal association, not direct identification or causal testing of a specific algorithmic circuit.
rows.check: The 'second descent always precedes onset' statement pools delayed-robustness and delayed-generalization runs. Only Figs 7/29 (scaled init) and 8 (modular addition) involve test-set grokking. It is a temporal association with a spline-region measure, not circuit identification.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated accuracy on test-set adversarial examples generated with ℓ∞-PGD during training.
rows.value: The network starts grokking adversarial examples after 10^4 optimization steps and attains almost equal robustness and generalization performance after 2 × 10^5 steps.
rows.note: The reported delayed outcome is adversarial robustness; the authors describe ordinary test accuracy as converging before this.
rows.check: Measures adversarial accuracy (delayed robustness), not delayed test generalization. The caption says this happens after test accuracy has converged. Moved to fits_no_version.

rows.note: The figure also displays clean training and test accuracy, but no exact values are stated in the text.
rows.check: Delayed robustness, not test-set grokking. The Fig 7 caption says this network does not undergo delayed generalization.

rows.subject: 4-layer ReLU MLP, width 200
rows.operation_detail: Scaled randomly initialized parameters by eight.
rows.measure: Test and adversarial accuracy over optimization steps
rows.value: The authors state that test-set grokking is visible and robustness periodically increases.
rows.note: The paper says this setup induces grokking; it does not provide a comparison against an unscaled initialization in the cited description.
rows.check: The baseline should be the unscaled MNIST MLP of Fig 2, which the paper says does not undergo delayed generalization. Scaling init by 8 induces visible test-set grokking (Fig 7). This replicates Liu et al.'s init-scale switch.

source_check.correct: Baseline: the unscaled MNIST MLP in Figure 2 does not undergo delayed test generalization. Scaling initialization by eight induces test-set grokking and periodically increasing robustness in Figure 7.
source_check.problem: The baseline is available: Figure 7 explicitly refers to Figure 2 as a setting without delayed generalization.

rows.subject: CNN with batch-normalization layers after every convolution
rows.operation_detail: Added batch-normalization layers after convolutional layers.

conditions.value: same setting as Figure 6-left without batch normalization

rows.measure: Adversarial accuracy and local complexity over optimization steps
rows.baseline: Without batch normalization, delayed adversarial grokking is reported.
rows.value: The authors state that grokking does not occur for adversarial samples; Table 1 says it does not occur or is significantly delayed.
rows.note: The paper describes batch normalization as removing grokking in this setting.
rows.check: Batch norm removes adversarial grokking (delayed robustness), not test-set grokking. Belongs in fits_no_version.

rows.subject: CNN, depth 5 and width 32
rows.measure: Local complexity and timing of region migration / adversarial grokking
rows.value: Weight decay does not have a monotonic effect: depending on its amount, it both delays and hastens region migration.
rows.note: The paper does not measure whether weight decay favors a more efficient generalizing circuit or test the proposed critical-size prediction.
rows.check: Reports the timing of local-complexity region migration, not any grokking rate. The setting is inconsistent: Section 4 says CIFAR10 CNN, while the Fig 30 caption and Table 1 say MNIST MLP. Table 1 says weight decay 'Delayed' adversarial grokking, but the text calls the effect non-monotonic. Not a test of V5's efficiency account.

rows.subject: MLP, depth 4 and width 200
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of training samples and evaluated adversarial performance during training.
rows.value: The paper states that increasing dataset size makes the network grok earlier.
rows.note: This reports the direction of the effect, but not a critical dataset size or ungrokking below a threshold.
rows.check: The dataset-size effect is on adversarial accuracy (Fig 28), not test accuracy. Fig 33 shows clean test accuracy for these sizes without test-set grokking. It does not test a critical dataset size or ungrokking.

relationships.reason: The authors report grokking occurring in this setting (R1). Evidence is figure-only, with no values or data-size sweep, so it is weak.

relationships.reason: A continuous measure (the LC second descent) is stated always to precede grokking onset (R1, R2). This anticipates the jump, but the measure is not a circuit-level mechanism.

source_check.condition: Standard-init CNN/ResNet on CIFAR10, CIFAR100, Imagenette and GPT on Shakespeare
